x-fc-resources.title: SDK resources
x-fc-resources.description: Which operation of the spec each method of each resource is. The same resources, methods and operations as funnelchat-node 0.3.2 (src/resources/*.ts, feat/seguir-un-grupo @ f913feb), with Python names (`sendDirect` -> `send_direct`). `python scripts/generate.py` builds src/funnelchat/resources.py from this and from the spec: the path parameters, query, body and response of each method come from the operation. If an operation of this list is no longer in the spec, the generation fails and says which one.

fields.mixins: Hand-written classes the resource also inherits from (`module:Class`).
fields.methods[].name: The method name, in snake_case.
fields.methods[].paginate: Returns a Page (iterate it for every item of every page) instead of the response body.
fields.methods[].doc: The method docstring. It starts with the operation in backticks.
fields.methods[].query: `false` leaves out the query keyword arguments of the operation (`extra_query` still works).
fields.methods[].bodyDefaults: Body fields that, when not given, take the value of a path parameter (so they are optional).
fields.methods[].pathNames: The Python name of a path parameter, when its snake_case name says less (`group` -> `group_uid`). Path parameters are positional-only, so the name never changes a call.
fields.methods[].idempotent: The operation takes `idempotency_key`, sent as the `Idempotency-Key` header.

resources.doc:
Messages to one contact (conversations area): send text, files, buttons and forms, read the history or one message by id, forward, react.

Every send answers right away with the registered message, `status` `queued`: accepted is not delivered. The rest arrives by `message.status_changed` (its `message_id` is the `id` of the message) or with `get()`. Sending with an API key needs **Contacts and conversations → Send** and follows the WhatsApp rules: `422 window_closed`, `422 antiblock_*`, `422 recipient_*`, `422 provider_unsupported`, `429 rate_limited` (with `retry_after`) and `429 mac_lockout_24h`. A rejected send stores nothing (see `SEND_ERROR_CODES`). A send is never retried automatically unless you pass `retry_send=True`.

methods.name: send
methods.doc:
`POST /api/v1/contacts/{contact}/message`: text, a file (`file`, a URL) or buttons and lists (`options`) to a contact. Returns `{"message": ...}`: the registered message, with its `id` and `status` `queued`.

Send `phone` (or `whatsapp_id`) of the same contact: the API checks it (`422 recipient_mismatch`). `contact_id` defaults to the contact of the route. A file from a URL without a known extension (a signed URL) needs `file_type` (`image`, `video`, `audio`, `document`, `sticker`), and a document `file_name`; an unsupported extension without `file_type` is a `415`. `client_reference` (1 to 64 visible ASCII characters) comes back in the history and in `message.status_changed`.

methods.name: send_direct
methods.doc:
`POST /api/v1/message/send-message`: a send straight to a phone, in one call: `device_id`, `phone` (with country code, digits only) and the text or file. If the phone is not a contact yet, it is created in the workspace of your key (as `contacts.upsert()` would), and it stays created even if a WhatsApp rule then stops the send. Returns `{"message": ...}`, with the contact in `message["contact_id"]`.

Instead of `phone`: `contact_id`, or `whatsapp_id` (Meta's id of the person, official numbers only). With `phone` and `contact_id`, they must be the same contact (`422 recipient_mismatch`); a phone of a contact of another workspace answers `404`. It is a send: same rules as `send()`.

methods.name: send_form
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/contacts/{contact}/message/form`: sends a published WhatsApp form (`form_id` is the form's `family_id`). Returns `{"message": ...}` with `type` `whatsapp_form`; the answers arrive by `whatsapp_form.completed`. It is a send: same rules as `send()`.

methods.name: get
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/contacts/{contact}/messages/{message}`: one message by the id a send or a webhook gave you (`message_id` of `message.status_changed`). `status` moves from `queued` to `sent`, `delivered`, `read` or `failed` (then `error` says why).

methods.name: list
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/contacts/{contactId}/messages`, paginated by cursor: the history of a contact.

methods.name: send_contact_card
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/contacts/{contact}/message/contact-card`: sends up to 5 contact cards. Returns `{"messages": [...]}`, one message per card, in the order of `contact_card_ids`.

methods.name: forward
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/contacts/{contact}/messages/{message}/forward`: forwards a message to up to 5 contacts. Returns one item per destination, in order: `status` (`queued`, or `blocked` with `reason`) and its `message`, or `None` when nothing was registered for that destination.

methods.name: react
methods.doc: `PUT /api/v1/contacts/{contact}/messages/{message}/reaction`: reacts with an emoji.

methods.name: remove_reaction
methods.doc: `DELETE /api/v1/contacts/{contact}/messages/{message}/reaction`: removes your reaction.

resources.doc: WhatsApp message templates (conversations area): list, create, edit, send.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/templates`, paginated. Send only the templates with `available` true: Meta pauses or disables the others.

methods.name: sync
methods.doc:
`POST /api/v1/devices/{device}/templates`: brings into Funnelchat the templates an official number has in Meta: those created or changed directly in Meta, which otherwise arrive only with the daily sync; it also removes those of a WhatsApp Business account the number no longer uses. Returns `{"status": "completed"}` when it is done, or `{"status": "in_progress"}` when the first page (up to 100) is in and the rest keeps coming in the background: list again with `list()`, in a few seconds for `in_progress`. Official numbers only.

Rejections (`TEMPLATE_SYNC_ERROR_CODES`): `404` (the number does not exist or is outside the key's workspace), `409 template_sync_in_progress` (one is already running for that number: do not start another), `422 number_not_connected_to_meta` (a QR number, or one without a WhatsApp Business account or credentials), `422 meta_rejected` (Meta refused and nothing was brought; its code in `error.body["meta_code"]`) and `502 meta_unavailable` (Meta did not answer).

methods.name: create
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/templates`: creates a template and submits it to Meta.

methods.name: retrieve
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/templates/{template}`.

methods.name: update
methods.doc: `PUT /api/v1/templates/{template}`.

methods.name: quick_reply_buttons
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/templates/{template}/quick-reply-buttons`.

methods.name: send
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/devices/{device}/templates/{template}/send-template`: sends an approved template, the way to write to a contact outside the 24-hour window. Send `phone` alone (the contact is created when it does not exist, as with `messages.send_direct()`), or `contact_id`, or both when they are the same contact; `template_variables` `{"body": [...]}` fills the body variables in order. Returns `{"message": ...}`, the registered message with `status` `queued`. A variable that points to a field that does not exist is `422 template_unresolved_placeholder`; a template this account cannot send, `404 template_not_found`. It is a send: never retried automatically.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: `DELETE /api/v1/devices/{device}/templates/{template}`.

resources.doc:
WhatsApp forms (conversations area): build them, version and publish them, choose their numbers and read the answers. To send one to a contact, `messages.send_form()`.

A form has versions: the `{id}` routes take a version id, the `families/{familyId}` routes the form's id (`family_id`). Reading needs **Contacts and conversations → View** and changing **Contacts and conversations → Edit**. The answers also arrive by `whatsapp_form.completed`.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/forms`, paginated: one row per form, with its current version.

methods.name: templates
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/forms/templates`: the templates to start a form from (`blank` is an empty one).

methods.name: create
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/forms`: creates a draft from a template (`template_key`) for a number.

methods.name: retrieve
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/forms/{id}`: one version (`id` is the version id), with its lint issues, versions and numbers.

methods.name: update
methods.doc: `PUT /api/v1/forms/{id}`: saves a draft. A published version answers `409 PUBLISHED`; with `expected_updated_at`, someone else's change answers `409 STALE`.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: `DELETE /api/v1/forms/{id}`: deletes a draft (a published form is deprecated, not deleted).

methods.name: create_version
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/forms/{id}/versions`: a new draft from this version, or the draft that already existed (`created` false).

methods.name: sync
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/forms/{id}/sync`: validates the version in Meta (`502 META` when Meta rejects it).

methods.name: publish
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/forms/{id}/publish`: publishes the version (`422 LINT` with errors).

methods.name: numbers
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/forms/{id}/numbers`: the numbers of the form and their state.

methods.name: add_number
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/forms/{id}/numbers`: adds a number.

methods.name: remove_number
methods.doc: `DELETE /api/v1/forms/{id}/numbers/{deviceId}`: removes a number (not the primary one).

methods.name: retry_numbers
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/forms/{id}/numbers/retry`: retries the numbers that failed.

methods.name: definition
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/forms/families/{familyId}/definition`: the published definition of a form, or `data` `None`.

methods.name: versions
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/forms/families/{familyId}/versions`: the versions of a form.

methods.name: list_responses
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/forms/families/{familyId}/responses`, paginated: the answers to a form, with `columns`.

methods.name: retrieve_response
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/forms/families/{familyId}/responses/{runId}`: one answer in detail.

methods.name: metrics
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/forms/families/{familyId}/metrics`: the funnel: sent, delivered, read, completed and the rates.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/tags`, paginated.

methods.name: create

methods.name: retrieve

methods.name: update

methods.name: list_contacts

resources.doc:
WhatsApp groups (communities area): the groups of a number, live from WhatsApp (`list_by_device()`); following one (`follow()`), so its joins and leaves arrive as events; sending a message to a group (`send_message()`) and reading how it went (`retrieve_action()`); and the groups already in the account, with their participants, joins and leaves, messages, scheduled messages and actions.

Reading needs **Groups and campaigns → View**, sending **Groups and campaigns → Send** and following **Groups and campaigns → Manage groups**. Who joins and who leaves a followed group arrives by `group_participant.joined` and `group_participant.left`.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/groups`, paginated: the groups already in the account. Each group's `uid` (`…@g.us`) is what `send_message()` takes.

methods.name: retrieve
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/groups/{group}`.

methods.name: list_by_device
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/devices/{device}/groups`, paginated (`page`, `pageSize`): the groups of one number, read live from WhatsApp (for a key, reused for a minute per number), also those not in the account yet. A group already in the account brings `device_id`; any other can be followed with `follow()`. Its `uid` is the group of `follow()` and `send_message()`.

methods.name: metadata
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/groups/{groupUid}/metadata`: live metadata of a group by its WhatsApp uid, read through one number.

methods.name: list_participants
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/groups/participants`, paginated: the participants of one group (`groupUid`).

methods.name: list_participant_events
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/groups/{group}/participant-events`, paginated: joins and leaves.

methods.name: list_messages
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/groups/{group}/messages`, paginated.

methods.name: list_scheduled_messages
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/groups/{group}/scheduled-messages`, paginated.

methods.name: list_actions
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/groups/{group}/actions`, paginated.

methods.name: send_message
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/groups/{group}/messages`: sends a text (`type="text"`, `text`) or one file (`image`, `video`, `audio` or `document`, by its `https` `media_url`) to the group with that `uid` (`…@g.us`), from `device_id`. It answers `202` with `{"action_id": ..., "status": "queued"}` and goes out in the background: the result arrives by `group_action.completed` (or `group_action.failed`), with the same `action_id` in `action.uuid`, or with `retrieve_action()`. A QR number must be admin of the group; an official number, the one the group belongs to. A group not in the account yet is followed first (`follow()`, with its rules). Rejections: `GROUP_ACTION_ERROR_CODES`. It is a send: never retried automatically.

methods.name: follow
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/groups/{group}/import`: follows the WhatsApp group with that `uid` (`…@g.us`) of a QR number (`device_id`), as importing it in the panel does: from then on its joins and leaves arrive by `group_participant.joined` and `group_participant.left`. Returns `{"data": {"uid", "name", "imported", "is_admin"}}`: `imported` is false when the group was already in the account, and `is_admin` says whether the number administers it (without that it cannot write to it). Needs **Groups and campaigns → Manage groups** (`403 import_permission_required`); up to 5 groups per number per minute (`429 import_rate_limited`, with `retry_after`); an official number is `422 provider_unsupported`.

methods.name: retrieve_action
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/groups/actions/{action}`: where a group action, such as a message sent with `send_message()`, is (`queued`, `running`, `completed` or `failed`) and its `result` (`result.message.uid` is the id of the message in WhatsApp).

resources.doc: WhatsApp numbers of the account (accounts area). The `id` of a number is the `device_id` you send with.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/devices`. `external_reference` keeps only the numbers with that reference (exact match).

methods.name: create
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/devices`: creates a number that connects by QR code (`connection="qr"`), not connected yet. Then show its QR with `qr()`, or send your customer a connect link (`connect_links.create()`). It takes a slot of the plan, with the panel's rejections (`403 numbers_not_included`, `403 number_limit_reached`…). An account has at most one QR number waiting to be scanned: another one is `409 pending_number_exists`, with that number's `device_id` in `error.body`. `country` (two letters) is the country of the phone that will scan the QR.

methods.name: retrieve
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/devices/{device}`. `capabilities` says what the number can do by API.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: `DELETE /api/v1/devices/{device}`: deletes the number and frees its slot of the plan. Irreversible. Sends `device.deleted`.

methods.name: update
methods.doc: `PUT /api/v1/devices/{device}`: also changes `external_reference`.

methods.name: qr
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/devices/{device}/qr`: the QR code to scan, as a PNG data URI (`qr_code`), or `None` once `connected`. Ask for it again every `expires_in` seconds and have it scanned right away: WhatsApp changes the code every few seconds, so show the latest and never store or forward a QR. Only for QR numbers (an official one is `422 provider_unsupported`).

methods.name: status
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/devices/{device}/status`: connection status.

methods.name: health
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/devices/{device}/health`.

methods.name: me
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/devices/{device}/me`: the WhatsApp profile of the number.

methods.name: check_phone
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/devices/{device}/check-phone`: whether a phone has WhatsApp.

methods.name: list_connection_history
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/devices/{device}/connection-history`, paginated.

resources.doc:
Connect links (accounts area): a single-use page, on the Funnelchat domain, where you or your customer connect a WhatsApp number to your account, by QR code (`type="qr"`) or as an official number through Meta's sign-up (`type="meta"`, answered `503 meta_connect_disabled` in production for now). The number is created when the page finishes; with `device_id` the link reconnects that number instead.

Reading needs **WhatsApp numbers → View**; creating and revoking, **WhatsApp numbers → Create, connect and delete**. The result arrives three ways: the `device.connected` webhook (with `connect_link_id` and `external_reference`), the `return_url`, or `get()`.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/connect-links`: returns `{"data": link}`. `link["url"]` is the page to open: it carries the token and comes only in this response. `country` (only `qr`, two letters) is the country of the phone that will scan the QR. At most 20 links open (`429 too_many_open_links`).

methods.name: get
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/connect-links/{link}`: its `status` (`pending`, `completed`, `failed`, `expired`, `revoked`), and `device_id` and `error_code` once it ends.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/connect-links`, paginated, newest first: filter by `status` or `external_reference`.

methods.name: revoke
methods.doc: `DELETE /api/v1/connect-links/{link}`: revokes a `pending` link (any other is `409 link_not_pending`).

resources.doc:
Webhook subscriptions (accounts area), plus `verify()` and `construct_event()` for the deliveries (the same functions as `funnelchat.webhooks`).

Reading needs **Notifications (webhooks) → View** and the rest **Notifications (webhooks) → Manage**. A key only sees and manages subscriptions to events of the areas it can read (**Contacts and conversations → View**, **Groups and campaigns → View**, **WhatsApp numbers → View**): asking for others is a `422` on `events`.

methods.name: events
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/webhooks/events`: the event types you can subscribe to, each with `status`.

methods.name: list
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/webhooks`: every subscription of the workspace of the key (at most 50), not only yours.

methods.name: create
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/webhooks`: the response brings `secret` once. Store it, and store the `id`.

methods.name: retrieve
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/webhooks/{id}` (without the secret).

methods.name: update
methods.doc: `PUT /api/v1/webhooks/{id}`: replaces `url`, `events`, `description` and `filters`. The secret stays.

methods.name: delete
methods.doc: `DELETE /api/v1/webhooks/{id}`.

methods.name: rotate_secret
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/rotate-secret`: the new secret comes once; the old one stops working. Not open to API keys (`403 route_not_available`): rotate it from the panel.

methods.name: test
methods.doc: `POST /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/test`: delivers one signed `webhook.test` now. Check `succeeded`.

methods.name: list_deliveries
methods.doc: `GET /api/v1/webhooks/{id}/deliveries`, paginated: one row per attempt, newest first.
